name: Component Gallery Comparative Patterns — Wave 1
purpose: Use cross-system prevalence and documentation signals to prioritize which behaviors deserve deeper Vault contracts. Counts are research metadata, not reuse permission.

vaultTakeaways: Modal is a mature cross-system pattern with unusually strong accessibility and usage-guidance coverage.
Treat alert/confirm/input dialogs as task-specific dialog variants rather than visual skins.
Focus management, dismissal, title/description semantics and action priority belong in the canonical contract.
Select is a form-value selection pattern and must remain distinct from action/navigation dropdown menus.
Native and custom selects may coexist; custom behavior must justify its complexity and preserve keyboard/value semantics.
Filtering belongs to combobox/autocomplete rather than being silently added to every select.
Distinguish semantic tables from application grids; sorting/selection/filtering change the interaction contract.
Responsive handling is a design decision: horizontal scroll, priority columns, detail disclosure or alternate mobile view must be explicit.
Do not replace dense comparable data with card soup solely for mobile aesthetics.
Dropzone is an enhancement, not the only upload mechanism; a keyboard-operable file input path remains required.
The contract must include selected-file state, validation, upload progress, failure/retry, removal and size/type constraints.
Do not imply successful upload until the server has accepted the file.
